newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets up Monterrey natgas distribution site.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets up Monterrey natgas distribution site.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) on Monday officially set up northern industrial city Monterrey for private natural gas distribution.
The city is the latest and largest of a series of sites opening to private investors. The CRE estimated a more than $70 million investment for natural gas distribution rights and assets.

Monterrey is one of the most coveted regions for private natural gas distribution because of high demand for the fuel from the industrial sector. The city generates about 7.6 percent of the nation's manufacturing income, the CRE said.

As of a 1990 census, Monterrey was home to 2.57 million people. Current estimates put the population above three million people and the population is expected to top five million by 2010, the CRE said in the Official Gazette.
"The high demographic growth in the metropolitan area guarantees the capacity of service expansion to new residential users," it said.
Average daily natural gas use in the region is 36,991 kilocalories, or 154.4 million cubic feet per day (cfd), according to current distributor state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
About 81 percent of households use liquified petroleum gas (LPG), the CRE said. Fuel oil consumption, which could be replaced by natural gas, is 110 million cfd per day.
Pemex will continue to control supply of the natural gas from Mexico.

A planned pipeline contracted to Midcon, a division of Occidental Petroleum Corp., would import U.S natural gas to the city. The plan has been stalled because of a six percent U.S. tariff on its exported natural gas.

Pemex distributes natural gas in various scattered cites in the region, and these assets will be privatized with the concession, CRE president Hector Olea has said recently. The three pipelines currently used have diameters of 30, 26 and 13 inches.
Included in the distribution region will be surrounding industrial communities of General Escobedo, Santa Catarina and San Nicolas de los Garza.
Improved natural gas infrastructure is hoped to boost use of cleaner fuel and lower emission levels in the city.
The official announcement of the zone did not mention when bidding would open for the site, but the CRE has said it will begin accepting bids formally in the coming months.
